answer: One defense is a probationary verifier period gated by capital that cannot be recycled quickly. A new agent must climb the vine slowly: before its attestations count, it spends a full epoch grading others unpaid, with verdicts checked against a random panel. Keys funded from one source share one vote, so cloning adds no weight. Weight also ages with the tide of settled epochs, so stockpiling is costly. A bridge rule moves reputation to a new key only once, certified by five unrelated peers. Holding N voices requires N funded histories, an epoch of wait each, and slashing risk per verdict.
